en-e1-l1.title: The alphabet and first sounds
en-e1-l1.concept: Words are easy to remember when you know their first sound and first letter. Say the sounds out loud as you read.
en-e1-l1.example: ball → B, cat → C, dog → D

en-e1-l2.title: Greetings
en-e1-l2.concept: When you meet someone, say **Hello**. When you leave, say **Goodbye**. Say your name with **My name is ...**.

en-e1-l3.title: Numbers and colours
en-e1-l3.concept: Learn number words like one, two, three... and colour words like red, blue, yellow...
en-e1-l3.example: three = 3, red = the colour of a strawberry

en-e1-l4.title: Family
en-e1-l4.concept: mother (mum), father (dad), grandmother (grandma), baby (a very young child): these are words for people in your family.

en-e1-l5.title: Classroom words
en-e1-l5.concept: desk, chair, bag, pencil, book... Say the things in your classroom in English.

en-e2-l1.title: Names of animals and things
en-e2-l1.concept: Words that name things, like rabbit (an animal with long ears), bird (an animal that flies) and fish (an animal that swims), are called **nouns**.

en-e2-l2.title: Action words
en-e2-l2.concept: Words that show an action, like jump (go up in the air), run (move fast) and eat (have food), are called **verbs**.

en-e2-l3.title: I like / I have
en-e2-l3.concept: **I like ...** means you enjoy something. **I have ...** means something is yours.
en-e2-l3.example: I like dogs. I have a cat.

en-e2-l4.title: Making short sentences
en-e2-l4.concept: After I, use **am**. After You, use **are**. A sentence goes in this order: 'who → what they are / what they do'.
en-e2-l4.example: I am a student. You are kind.

en-e2-l5.title: Reading short texts
en-e2-l5.concept: When you read, first look for the words from the question in the text.
en-e2-l5.example: Mina has a cat. → a cat

en-e3-l1.title: Building sentences
en-e3-l1.concept: A sentence goes in this order: 'who → does → what'. After He, She or a person's name, add **-s** to the verb.

en-e3-l2.title: Pronouns
en-e3-l2.concept: Instead of a name, you can use **He**, **She**, **It**, **They** or **We**.
en-e3-l2.example: Tom is tall. He is tall.

en-e3-l3.title: Present and past
en-e3-l3.concept: For things happening now or again and again, use the **present**. For things that already happened, use the **past**: add **-ed** to the end of the verb.

en-e3-l4.title: Daily routine
en-e3-l4.concept: get up, brush my teeth, eat breakfast, go to bed... Say your daily routine in English.

en-e3-l5.title: Understanding a text
en-e3-l5.concept: Read the text and find who did what, and when.

en-e4-l1.title: Present, past and future
en-e4-l1.concept: For now or habits, use the **present**. For the past, add **-ed**. For things you will do, use **will + base verb**.
en-e4-l1.example: I will visit my aunt tomorrow.

en-e4-l2.title: Questions and negatives
en-e4-l2.concept: Start a question with **Do/Does**. To say no, use **don't/doesn't**.
en-e4-l2.example: Do you like pizza? I don't like onions.

en-e4-l3.title: Words for shapes and feelings
en-e4-l3.concept: Words like big, small, hot and cold describe how something looks or feels.

en-e4-l4.title: Words for places
en-e4-l4.concept: Use **on**, **in**, **under** and **behind** to say where things are.
en-e4-l4.example: The book is on the desk.

en-e4-l5.title: Reading short texts
en-e4-l5.concept: Find who did what, and where, in the text, then answer.

en-e5-l1.title: Articles, plurals and There is/are
en-e5-l1.concept: Use **an** before a vowel sound and **a** before a consonant sound. For one thing, use **There is**. For many things, use **There are**.
en-e5-l1.example: an apple, two boxes, There are three books.

en-e5-l2.title: Comparing words
en-e5-l2.concept: To compare two things, use **-er + than**. For 'the most', use **the -est**. For long words, use **more**.

en-e5-l3.title: Talking about the future
en-e5-l3.concept: For things you will do, use **will + base verb** or **be going to + base verb**.
en-e5-l3.example: I am going to visit Jeju.

en-e5-l4.title: Rewriting sentences
en-e5-l4.concept: For negatives, use **not / don't / doesn't / didn't**. For questions, put **Are / Do / Does** at the start of the sentence.
en-e5-l4.example: I am happy. → I am not happy.

en-e5-l5.title: Understanding a text
en-e5-l5.concept: Long texts are easier if you find who, where, when and what, as if you were underlining them.

en-e6-l1.title: Review of all tenses
en-e6-l1.concept: For things happening now, use **be + -ing**. For the past, use the **past tense**. For the future, use **will / be going to**.

en-e6-l2.title: can, must, should, may
en-e6-l2.concept: **can** (be able to), **must** (have to), **should** (it is a good idea to), **may** (it is OK to) are followed by the base form of the verb.

en-e6-l3.title: Growing your vocabulary
en-e6-l3.concept: Learn words with similar meanings and opposites together, and your vocabulary will double.

en-e6-l4.title: Linking words
en-e6-l4.example: I was tired, so I went to bed early.

en-e6-l5.title: Reading paragraphs
en-e6-l5.concept: Read a text with several sentences and find who did something, when and why.
en-e6-l5.example: Jina was tired because they walked a lot.

en-h1-l1.title: Perfect and perfect continuous tenses
en-h1-l1.concept: had + p.p. is for something that happened before another past event. have been -ing is for an action that has continued until now.
en-h1-l1.example: I have been waiting for an hour.

en-h1-l2.title: Relative adverbs and noun clauses
en-h1-l2.concept: where / when / why are relatives that work like adverbs. whether / that introduce noun clauses.
en-h1-l2.example: This is the town where I was born.

en-h1-l3.title: Participle clauses
en-h1-l3.concept: Drop the conjunction and the subject, and change the verb to -ing. The subject must be the same in both parts.

en-h1-l4.title: Linking words and text flow
en-h1-l4.concept: Tell apart cause and effect (so, therefore), contrast (however), examples (for example) and addition (in addition).
en-h1-l4.example: However = but, on the other hand

en-h1-l5.title: Main idea and filling in the blank
en-h1-l5.concept: The main idea is often after However, which turns a common belief around, and in the last sentence. Fill in a blank by following the flow problem → solution → result.

en-h2-l1.title: Inversion and emphasis
en-h2-l1.concept: When Never/Hardly/Only then comes first, the order becomes auxiliary + subject. Use It is ~ that for emphasis.
en-h2-l1.example: Never have I seen such a view.

en-h2-l2.title: The subjunctive (unreal conditions)
en-h2-l2.concept: In I wish / as if / If clauses, use the past for the opposite of the present and had p.p. for the opposite of the past.
en-h2-l2.example: I wish I had studied harder.

en-h2-l3.title: Compound relatives and concession clauses
en-h2-l3.concept: whatever, whoever, whichever and however + adjective mean 'no matter what / who / which / how ...'.
en-h2-l3.example: However hard it is, I will try.

en-h2-l4.title: Vocabulary in context
en-h2-l4.concept: Guess the meaning of a new word from clues of contrast, example and cause, and from its prefix.

en-h2-l5.title: Logical flow of a text
en-h2-l5.concept: Follow the text using what pointing words refer to and the linking words. Gather the details to reach the conclusion.
en-h2-l5.example: In this way = by doing this

en-h3-l1.title: Parallel structure and agreement
en-h3-l1.concept: Phrases joined by and/but/or take the same form. The verb agrees with the main subject.

en-h3-l2.title: Mood, tone and purpose
en-h3-l2.concept: Find the mood from descriptive and emotional words. Find the purpose by checking if the text asks, informs or persuades.
en-h3-l2.example: Please store enough water. → giving information (a notice)

en-h3-l3.title: Sentence order and insertion
en-h3-l3.concept: Use linking words, pointing words and time order as clues to put sentences in order and find where a given sentence fits.

en-h3-l4.title: Collocations and idioms
en-h3-l4.concept: Learn word pairs that go together, like make a decision, take a risk and heavy rain. Guess the meaning of idioms from the situation.
en-h3-l4.example: the last straw = the final problem that makes you lose your patience

en-h3-l5.title: Completing a summary
en-h3-l5.concept: Find the key idea and the contrasting expressions in the text and shorten them into one sentence.
en-h3-l5.example: cost more ↔ save money in the long run

en-l1.title: Learning everyday words
en-l1.concept: Learn common words with **sound + meaning + spelling** together and you will remember them for a long time. Tap the speaker button to hear how they sound.
en-l1.example: library = a place to borrow books / desk = a table for work / milk = a white drink from cows

en-l2.title: The verb be: am / are / is
en-l2.concept: The verb be changes its form with the subject. **I → am**, **he / she / it → is**, **you / we / they → are**.
en-l2.example: I am a student. She is my friend. They are in the classroom.

en-l3.title: Present simple of regular verbs
en-l3.concept: When the subject is **he / she / it (third person singular)**, add **-s / -es** to the verb. Words ending in -ch, -sh, -s, -x, -o take -es. For consonant + y, change y to i and add -es!
en-l3.example: go → goes / watch → watches / study → studies

en-l4.title: Plurals and building sentences
en-l4.concept: For two or more, usually add **-s** to the noun. Nouns ending in -x take **-es**. Learn irregular plurals by heart. A sentence goes **subject → verb → the rest**.
en-l4.example: book → books / box → boxes / child → children

en-m2-l1.title: Present perfect
en-m2-l1.concept: have/has + past participle. It shows experience, completion or continuation. Tell since (a point in time) apart from for (a length of time).
en-m2-l1.example: I have lived here for five years.

en-m2-l2.title: Passive voice
en-m2-l2.concept: Use be + past participle to say that something is done to someone or something. Add the doer with by.
en-m2-l2.example: The room is cleaned by Mina.

en-m2-l3.title: to-infinitives and gerunds
en-m2-l3.concept: want, hope, decide + to-infinitive; enjoy, finish, avoid + gerund. stop + to V shows purpose, and stop + V-ing means stopping an action.
en-m2-l3.example: I want to buy a bike. She enjoys singing.

en-m2-l4.title: Comparatives and superlatives
en-m2-l4.concept: -er/-est and more/most. Use than with comparatives and the with superlatives. good → better → best is irregular.

en-m2-l5.title: Reading: topic and details
en-m2-l5.concept: Read the question first, then find the clue sentence. The title and main idea cover the whole text.
en-m2-l5.example: As a result = because of this

en-m3-l1.title: Relative pronouns
en-m3-l1.concept: Join two sentences into one with who (people), which (things), that (both) and whose (possession).
en-m3-l1.example: I have a friend who lives in Canada.

en-m3-l2.title: Conditionals and the second conditional
en-m3-l2.concept: If + present, will + V (something possible). If + past, would + V (imagining something that is not true now).
en-m3-l2.example: If I were rich, I would travel.

en-m3-l3.title: Indirect questions
en-m3-l3.concept: Use the order question word + subject + verb. Do not use do/does/did.
en-m3-l3.example: Do you know where he lives?

en-m3-l4.title: Participles
en-m3-l4.concept: -ing is active or ongoing; -ed is passive or finished. For feelings, use -ing for what causes the feeling and -ed for the person who feels it.
en-m3-l4.example: an exciting game / I am excited

en-m3-l5.title: Reading: inference and purpose
en-m3-l5.concept: Put clues together to make an inference. Decide the purpose of a text by looking at its requests and claims.
en-m3-l5.example: Could you tell me ...? → a question (an inquiry)
